questions.q: What does a bookmark capture about a report page?
options: Filters, slicer selections, cross-highlighting, sort order, drill position, and visibility of objects
Only the page's title
Only which visuals exist on the page, not their state
Only the report's overall theme colors
questions.explain: A bookmark is a snapshot of the page's entire interactive state — far more than just which page was active.

questions.q: Why might you turn off a bookmark's Data property?
options: Turning off Data disables the bookmark entirely
When using bookmarks to switch between different visual layouts rather than different filters, so switching views doesn't reset a viewer's filter selections
Data properties can never be turned off
To prevent the bookmark from being deleted
questions.explain: If Data stays on, applying the bookmark would reset filters and slicers along with the layout change — often not what you want for view-switching bookmarks.

questions.q: How do you assign a bookmark to a button?
options: Buttons and bookmarks are unrelated features with no way to connect them
Right-click the bookmark and select Assign to button
Bookmarks can only be triggered from the Bookmarks pane, never from a button
Insert a button, toggle Action on, set Type to Bookmark, and choose the bookmark from the dropdown
questions.explain: The Format button pane's Action section is where you connect a button to a specific bookmark, turning it into a one-click way to apply that saved state.

questions.q: What happens when you select View on a bookmark that belongs to a group?
options: The group is deleted
Every bookmark in the entire report plays, regardless of grouping
Only the bookmarks in that group play as a slideshow, not the entire report's bookmarks
The bookmark's Data and Display properties are automatically reset
questions.explain: Selecting View from within a group scopes the slideshow to just that group — useful for presenting a specific sequence of insights.

questions.q: What's the difference between a bookmark's 'All visuals' and 'Selected visuals' options?
options: 'Selected visuals' always includes every visual automatically
'All visuals' applies the bookmark's settings to every visual on the page; 'Selected visuals' applies them only to visuals chosen when the bookmark was created
'All visuals' only works with the Display property, never Data
There is no difference — both apply to the same visuals
questions.explain: This lets different bookmarks affect different parts of the same page — useful when you want several bookmarks to control separate sections independently.
